best_section: article: Abstract
new_text: Generative foundation models that combine natural language with omics data must decide how biology reaches the language model: by translating it into the model's own tokens or by encoding it with a biological model and injecting the result. In this scoping review (searches to 9 August 2026) we included 55 records describing 51 independent works, 109 models and 585 input routes, decomposed the routes into a library of 22 data operations and charted rationales, supervision, dependence tests and cross-representation comparisons. Seventeen works are token-native, 16 encoder-mediated and 8 hybrid, and 9 use language to condition a biology model. Token-native works keep a median of 100 gene names per cell, and only 2 of the 51 works write measured values as numbers. Works that inject encoder outputs give the language model 1–256 vectors per biological object, and a third of the route steps in the median encoder-mediated work are opaque learned modules. Twenty-five works train or evaluate on text written by another large language model, and only 22 test whether outputs depend on the biological input. In 31 cross-culture comparisons in 20 works, the authors' own representation won 28. Opponents were mostly released, unadapted forms of the other culture, and opponents trained by the proposing team lost all 11 comparisons. The two cultures keep complementary parts of biological data, and the published comparisons cannot yet tell which serves a given task better. We propose a neutral comparison protocol and a reporting card for input representations.

new_text: Where authors discuss the choice, they describe this trade-off the same way from both sides: token-native works cite unchanged architectures and the language model's knowledge of named entities and concede the loss of quantitative information, while encoder-mediated works criticise text rendering for that loss. The distinction itself is familiar. What has been missing is a measurement of its consequences and evidence about when each side of the trade-off matters.

old_text: **Objective.** To map generative text–omics foundation models by how they couple language and biology. For each design we ask what it keeps of the data, how it is justified, supervised and tested, and what the comparative evidence shows.

new_text: Recent surveys classify models by family, modality and task; LLM4Cell, for example, groups 58 single-cell methods into five methodological families and maps them to eight analytical tasks. [CITE, to verify: ACL 2025 survey of single-cell foundation language models; LLMs meet virtual cell; Nature 2025 perspective on multimodal foundation models in molecular cell biology; 2026 Cell Systems compositional-FM review; scoping review of LLM-generated synthetic data in biomedicine.] The translate-or-encode distinction is familiar to primary authors, who use it to justify their designs. This review measures, at the level of operations, what each design keeps and how its claims are tested, across omics modalities.

new_text: **Analysis.** Motifs are mined from route chains bounded by the charted transformation chains and from four author-curated pilot graphs, so steps that the charting did not record cannot form motifs. Support thresholds (at least 4 papers) and motif naming involved author judgement. The design-pattern axes are derived from the charted routes and their decomposition. Interface and carrier labels inherit charting errors, and the axis for the transformation of measured values falls back on the charted carrier subtype for 90 biological routes whose chain has no decided operation. The axes were defined by the authors after inspecting the data and were not validated on an independent corpus. Protocol objective 3 (datasets, downstream tasks, evaluation metrics) and the extraction fields for pretraining objective and code/data availability are not yet charted, except the evaluation formats and outputs recorded in the targeted pass. The design-culture analysis was defined after exploring the decomposed corpus, so its hypotheses are post hoc. Its charting used two runs of one model family and adjudication by a single steward. Run agreement was high for comparison presence (κ 0.92), LLM-generated text (κ 0.96) and dependence tests (Jaccard 0.91), but lower for evaluation formats (0.57) and rationales (0.60). A second human coder for the 31 comparison units and the culture assignment is planned before submission. Culture assignment for works that combine separate models is a judgement call; Geneverse is coded token-native, although its image models are encoder-mediated. Group sizes are small (17, 16, 8 and 9 works), and culture contrasts are exploratory (unadjusted Fisher tests). Comparisons are as reported by the authors; publication bias contributes to home advantage, so it is part of the finding as well as a limitation. Comparisons reported only in figures can be missed by the charting runs. While checking one exception (CellTosg2Sequence), we found a Tahoe-100M perturbation-classification comparison against C2S-Scale-27B, won by the proposer, that neither run charted; it is not counted. Such misses would add to home advantage, and the second-coder check will include a recall audit of comparisons. Gene and token budgets are taken from stated values in 8 and 11 works; works that do not state them are not counted. Earlier keyword pre-screens of the full texts (used to choose the variables for the targeted pass) skipped appendices after the reference list. new_text: Generative foundation models that combine natural language with omics data must decide how biology reaches the language model: by translating it into the model's own tokens or by encoding it with a biological model and injecting the result. In this scoping review (searches to 9 August 2026) we included 55 records describing 51 independent works, 109 models and 585 input routes, decomposed the routes into a library of 22 data operations and charted rationales, supervision, dependence tests and cross-representation comparisons. Seventeen works are token-native, 16 encoder-mediated and 8 hybrid, and 9 use language to condition a biology model. Token-native works keep a median of 100 gene names per cell, and only 2 of the 51 works write measured values as numbers. Works that inject encoder outputs give the language model 1–256 vectors per biological object, and a third of the route steps in the median encoder-mediated work are opaque learned modules. Twenty-five works train or evaluate on text written by another large language model, and only 22 test whether outputs depend on the biological input. In 31 cross-culture comparisons in 20 works, the authors' own representation won 28. Opponents were mostly released, unadapted forms of the other culture, and opponents trained by the proposing team lost all 11 comparisons. The two cultures keep complementary parts of biological data, and the published comparisons cannot yet tell which serves a given task better. We propose a neutral comparison protocol and a reporting card for input representations.

new_text: Generative foundation models that combine natural language with omics data must decide how biology reaches the language model: by translating it into the model's own tokens or by encoding it with a biological model and injecting the result. In this scoping review (searches to 9 August 2026) we included 55 records describing 51 independent works, 109 models and 585 input routes, decomposed the routes into a library of 22 data operations and charted rationales, supervision, dependence tests and cross-representation comparisons. Seventeen works are token-native, 16 encoder-mediated and 8 hybrid, and 9 use language to condition a biology model. Token-native works keep a median of 100 gene names per cell, and only 2 of the 51 works write measured values as numbers. Works that inject encoder outputs give the language model 1–256 vectors per biological object, and a third of the route steps in the median encoder-mediated work are opaque learned modules. Twenty-five works train or evaluate on text written by another large language model, and only 22 test whether outputs depend on the biological input. In 31 cross-culture comparisons in 20 works, the authors' own representation won 28. Opponents were mostly released, unadapted forms of the other culture, and opponents trained by the proposing team lost all 11 comparisons. The two cultures keep complementary parts of biological data, and the published comparisons cannot yet tell which serves a given task better. We propose a neutral comparison protocol and a reporting card for input representations.

new_text: Each documented input path was then reconstructed as a directed graph of calls to a library of 22 reusable operations (normalisation, log transform, binning, tokenisation, table lookup, projection, concatenation, attention and others) with named inputs and outputs and instance parameters. Steps whose internal computation the paper does not state remain unexpanded boundaries. A four-paper pilot (ChatNT, InstructCell, X-Cell, MUPAD; 47 trajectories, 509 operation calls) was curated by the authors. The remaining 50 papers were decomposed by an LLM agent in three independent runs per paper, with the structure fixed by the charted routes (one step per element of each route's transformation chain); the published decision for each step is the majority of the three runs, and every decision was checked mechanically for verbatim evidence, valid operation inputs and outputs, and declared parameters. A separate parameter pass then read the whole paper again, with the operations fixed. For every declared parameter of every operation call (2,433 slots) it decided whether the paper states the value for that data path, with verbatim evidence checked mechanically; values that only follow from convention, released code or cited papers do not count. This pass also used three runs per paper and the majority status, and its acceptance gate was fixed before the first run. The decomposition rules were developed on ten length-stratified papers and evaluated on held-out papers with the rules frozen (Supplementary Note S3). The result is version 1.3.0 of the operation library. The withdrawn OKR-Cell preprint was not decomposed.

new_text: The unit of charting is a grounded input route: one source object carried through its transformation chain to the representation that the model receives (the carrier). Routes were extracted from the full text with three frozen runs plus dense-coverage candidates and classified by carrier mechanism into five families and 15 subtypes. old_text: Each documented input path is reconstructed as a directed graph of calls to a library of 22 reusable operations (normalisation, log transform, binning, tokenisation, table lookup, projection, concatenation, attention and others) with named ports and instance parameters (`protocol/REPRESENTATION_LIBRARY_GUIDE.md`; catalog definitions of release 1.3.0). Steps whose internal computation the paper does not state remain unexpanded boundaries. A four-paper pilot (ChatNT, InstructCell, X-Cell, MUPAD; 47 trajectories, 509 operation calls) was curated by the authors. The remaining 50 papers were decomposed by agents (Codex CLI, `gpt-5.6-luna`, reasoning effort high; the earlier `gpt-5.4-mini` is no longer available through Codex) under protocol v3.2 (`scripts/operation_decomposition_v3.py`; v3.2 sharpens the boundaries between align, concatenate and serialize, and partition and select, after run-to-run disagreements under v3.1; `analysis/representation_block_library_2026-10-04/DECISION_MEMO_1.3.0.md`). The structure is fixed by the charted routes: one trajectory per charted configuration and one step per element of each route's verbatim transformation chain. For each step the agent returns only a decision, a closed category plus the library operation(s) named in the element text, with stated parameter values, verbatim evidence and the echoed chain element. A predefined rule set decides the category (e.g. unexpanded learned module, data provenance, external text generator, unspecified fusion). Routes without a recorded chain get a mechanical decision. Nodes, ports and data flow are compiled from these decisions, and the result is checked mechanically for verbatim evidence, catalog ports and declared parameters. The full paper text is supplied without truncation. Each paper was decomposed in three independent runs (up to four mechanical repairs each), and the published decision per step is the majority label. Steps without a majority remain unresolved boundaries and are listed for the library steward, as are steps decided 2 of 3. A separate parameter pass then read the whole paper again, with the operations fixed. For every declared parameter of every library call (2,433 slots in 1.3.0; definitions in `protocol/OPERATION_PARAMETER_GLOSSARY.md`) it decided whether the paper states the value for that data path, with verbatim evidence checked mechanically. Values that only follow from convention, released code or cited papers do not count. This pass also used three runs per paper and the majority status; its rules were tuned on the ten development papers (two iterations) and then frozen. Before the first run we fixed its gate: on ten held-out papers, consensus status agreement between runs 1-3 and 4-6 of at least 0.90 (`analysis/operation_decomposition_v31_2026-10-12/parameter_pass/GATE.md`). The result was library release 1.2.1. Under v3.2, 39 of 1,468 steps changed operation; the parameter pass was repeated for the 16 affected papers (three runs), and slots of unchanged calls were carried over. The result is library release 1.3.0. No reviewer-agent pass was run on it. The protocol was developed iteratively on ten length-stratified papers and evaluated on held-out papers with the rules frozen. Stability was measured as agreement between the consensus of runs 1-3 and of runs 4-6 against a predeclared gate (`analysis/operation_decomposition_2026-10-07/stabilization/GATE.md`, `STABILIZATION_REPORT.md`). The withdrawn OKR-Cell preprint is not included.

new_section: Abstract
best_section: article: Abstract
new_text: Generative foundation models that combine natural language with omics data must decide how biology reaches the language model: by translating it into the model's own tokens or by encoding it with a biological model and injecting the result. In this scoping review (searches to 9 August 2026) we included 55 records describing 51 independent works, 109 models and 585 input routes, decomposed the routes into a library of 22 data operations and charted rationales, supervision, dependence tests and cross-representation comparisons. Seventeen works are token-native, 16 encoder-mediated and 8 hybrid, and 9 use language to condition a biology model. Token-native works keep a median of 100 gene names per cell, and only 2 of the 51 works write measured values as numbers. Works that inject encoder outputs give the language model 1–256 vectors per biological object, and a third of the route steps in the median encoder-mediated work are opaque learned modules. Twenty-five works train or evaluate on text written by another large language model, and only 22 test whether outputs depend on the biological input. In 31 cross-culture comparisons in 20 works, the authors' own representation won 28. Opponents were mostly released, unadapted forms of the other culture, and opponents trained by the proposing team lost all 11 comparisons. The two cultures keep complementary parts of biological data, and the published comparisons cannot yet tell which serves a given task better. We propose a neutral comparison protocol and a reporting card for input representations.

old_text: **Why "cultures".** We use the term for a bundle of choices that travel together, not for the input route alone. Two parts of the bundle follow from the definition: what reaches the language model (§3.5) and the motif families above, which are mined from the same routes. Two do not: the stated justifications, which describe the same trade-off from opposite sides (§3.6), and the choice of opponents, which differs sharply by proposing culture (§3.9). new_text: **Token-native routes keep identities and order and drop magnitudes** (Figure 4a; Supplementary Table S7). Works that write transcriptomes as text keep 50–1000 genes per cell, with a median of 100 over the 8 works that state this number (K). The genes are listed in rank order: Cell2Sentence, CellHermes, ChatCell and TeamPath keep 100, CellTosg2Sequence 200, and C2S-Scale reports that 1000 often works well. OCellus' spatial prefix keeps 5 marker genes per neighbour. Values are written as numbers in only 2 works (CpG beta values, blood-biomarker values). Rank tie handling is never stated (0 of 24 ranking calls), and selection forced inclusions are stated in none of 105 selection calls. Two works report that within-cell rank tracks log-expression (Cell2Sentence; CellTosg2Sequence, R² ≈ 0.90). If so, what a cell sentence cannot recover is mainly the genes outside the top K (at least 95% of about 20,000 genes when K ≤ 1000), the order among ties, and any cell-specific departure from the population-level fit between rank and expression.

new_text: **Encoder routes pass magnitudes to learned modules and hide what survives.** Encoder routes in the six works that state their input size use 331–20,541 features (median about 2,800). Eleven works with soft-token or query interfaces deliver each biological object to the downstream model as 1–256 vectors (median 32): 1 (BIOVERSE, OmicsLM), 8 (InstructCell, Genolator), 10 discrete codes (RVQ-Alpha), 32 (scMMGPT, SciCore-Omics, Bio-BLIP, scMIR), 200 (CellTosg2Sequence) and 256 (scMOBA). For comparison, Cell2Sentence spends about 350 text tokens on a prompt plus 100 genes. By culture, these counts are: token-native works K = 50–1000 (5 works; hybrids 100–250, 3 works); encoder-mediated works 1–256 vectors (median 32, 7 works) from 2,048–20,541 features (3 works). In the median encoder-mediated work, 0.33 of biological route steps are opaque learned modules, against 0 in the median token-native work (Figure 4b). The projector activation is unstated in 82% of encoder-projector motifs and the concatenation order in 95% of encode-then-join motifs.

new_text: Generative foundation models that combine natural language with omics data must decide how biology reaches the language model: by translating it into the model's own tokens or by encoding it with a biological model and injecting the result. In this scoping review (searches to 9 August 2026) we included 55 records describing 51 independent works, 109 models and 585 input routes, decomposed the routes into a library of 22 data operations and charted rationales, supervision, dependence tests and cross-representation comparisons. Seventeen works are token-native, 16 encoder-mediated and 8 hybrid, and 9 use language to condition a biology model. Token-native works keep a median of 100 gene names per cell, and only 2 of the 51 works write measured values as numbers. Works that inject encoder outputs give the language model 1–256 vectors per biological object, and a third of the route steps in the median encoder-mediated work are opaque learned modules. Twenty-five works train or evaluate on text written by another large language model, and only 22 test whether outputs depend on the biological input. In 31 cross-culture comparisons in 20 works, the authors' own representation won 28. Opponents were mostly released, unadapted forms of the other culture, and opponents trained by the proposing team lost all 11 comparisons. The two cultures keep complementary parts of biological data, and the published comparisons cannot yet tell which serves a given task better. We propose a neutral comparison protocol and a reporting card for input representations.

new_text: **Analysis.** Motifs are mined from route chains bounded by the charted transformation chains and from four author-curated pilot graphs, so steps that the charting did not record cannot form motifs. Support thresholds (at least 4 papers) and motif naming involved author judgement. The design-pattern axes are derived from the charted routes and their decomposition. Interface and carrier labels inherit charting errors, and the axis for the transformation of measured values falls back on the charted carrier subtype for 90 biological routes whose chain has no decided operation. The axes were defined by the authors after inspecting the data and were not validated on an independent corpus. Protocol objective 3 (datasets, downstream tasks, evaluation metrics) and the extraction fields for pretraining objective and code/data availability are not yet charted, except the evaluation formats and outputs recorded in the targeted pass. The design-culture analysis was defined after exploring the decomposed corpus, so its hypotheses are post hoc. Its charting used two runs of one model family and adjudication by a single steward. Run agreement was high for comparison presence (κ 0.92), LLM-generated text (κ 0.96) and dependence tests (Jaccard 0.91), but lower for evaluation formats (0.57) and rationales (0.60). A second human coder for the 31 comparison units and the culture assignment is planned before submission. Culture assignment for works that combine separate models is a judgement call; Geneverse is coded token-native, although its image models are encoder-mediated. Group sizes are small (17, 16, 8 and 9 works), and culture contrasts are exploratory (unadjusted Fisher tests). Comparisons are as reported by the authors; publication bias contributes to home advantage, so it is part of the finding as well as a limitation. new_text: **Search and selection.** Open access and English were required. At search they were applied only in PubMed (with "free full text" as a proxy for open access), Scopus and OpenAlex, and elsewhere at screening. On 2026-10-14 we re-ran the baseline queries of PubMed, arXiv, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar for the window; they returned 51 unique records, 17 had already been retrieved, and none of the other 34 met the eligibility criteria in an indicative single-pass LLM title/abstract triage. Scopus and Springer Nature were not re-run. new_text: Each documented input path was then reconstructed as a directed graph of calls to a library of 22 reusable operations (normalisation, log transform, binning, tokenisation, table lookup, projection, concatenation, attention and others) with named inputs and outputs and instance parameters. Steps whose internal computation the paper does not state remain unexpanded boundaries. A four-paper pilot (ChatNT, InstructCell, X-Cell, MUPAD; 47 trajectories, 509 operation calls) was curated by the authors. The remaining 50 papers were decomposed by an LLM agent in three independent runs per paper, with the structure fixed by the charted routes (one step per element of each route's transformation chain); the published decision for each step is the majority of the three runs, and every decision was checked mechanically for verbatim evidence, valid operation inputs and outputs, and declared parameters. A separate parameter pass then read the whole paper again, with the operations fixed. For every declared parameter of every operation call (2,433 slots) it decided whether the paper states the value for that data path, with verbatim evidence checked mechanically; values that only follow from convention, released code or cited papers do not count. This pass also used three runs per paper and the majority status, and its acceptance gate was fixed before the first run. The decomposition rules were developed on ten length-stratified papers and evaluated on held-out papers with the rules frozen (Supplementary Note S3). The result is version 1.3.0 of the operation library. The withdrawn OKR-Cell preprint was not decomposed.
